transcript.content: Hello, it's nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Nice to meet you too. Well, I'm here because... I think I need some help. After I eat too much, I keep going to the bathroom and making myself throw up. I just do it so I won't gain weight, but it's... it's gotten to the point where I'm honestly scared I can't stop doing it.
In a typical week, how many times do you make yourself vomit after eating?

Well, for at least the past three months, there's hardly been a week where I didn't have one of those late-night eating episodes and then go make myself throw up afterward. Some weeks it happens several times... especially when I'm home more because of my back.
During these late-night episodes, do you eat an unusually large amount of food—more than most people would eat in similar circumstances?

Yeah, I do. It's... it's definitely a lot more than a normal meal. Usually at night, after everyone's gone quiet, I'll just stand in the kitchen and eat whatever's there. Leftovers, cereal, chips, ice cream... I just keep going, way past what anyone would call a normal amount, until half the pantry just looks picked over.
How much do your weight or body shape affect how you judge yourself as a person?

It affects me a lot, honestly. Like... if my work pants start feeling tight, or if I happen to catch a look at my belly in the mirror, I just feel like I’m failing at everything. 

I'm a mechanic, and I've always prided myself on being this strong woman who could handle pulling out heavy transmissions and keeping up with all the guys in the shop. But when I don't like how my body looks or feels, it just... it completely ruins how I see myself. It makes me feel like I'm not that strong person anymore, and it's hard not to judge myself for it.
